items.title: Albert Warner Interview, 1959-01-08
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...I know that he wasn't a man on my top or Hashton Bond, you understand? ... Oh, yes. But he was a good man, you understand? Just like Jim.

ctx.x: Well, what is he, a real teen? Yeah. You see, that's the thing I didn't know. I'm telling you, right back in those days, I didn't know. All I'd know, I used to just go to the dancers, they could sit down there and play it. I wouldn't know if he was playing my head or not.

I know as a little guy, but not too much, I understand. But I know that he wasn't a man on my top or Hashton Bond, you understand? Or Lewis Nelson, he wasn't on the top of them. Oh, yes. But he was a good man, you understand? Just like Jim. Now, what did he do, what did he call me? Jim. He said, hello, Mr. Jim. I said, hello. But my name is not Jim. But I used to say, Jim. I said, okay. I said, how you feeling? Okay. Because he said, I'm Jim. He said, brother, of course, we kind of feel with him. And when we…
You taught him drum on and taught him how to talk too?
